items.title: Moburst develops AI engine optimization capabilities for established companies - TechCrunch
items.summary: Mobile growth agency Moburst has built out a dedicated AI Engine Optimization practice aimed at established companies with existing app portfolios, betting that the category still lacks agencies with real depth rather than a rebranded service page. AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. For established companies vetting an AEO partner, the practical test is whether the agency can point to specific app-store-side work, not just web content changes, and whether it can describe a concrete process for reconciling inconsistent brand descriptions across many independent sources rather than treating that as someone else’s problem.

items.title: 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development' - Business Insider
items.summary: # Over 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development'. Senior officials at some of the nation's leading AI companies say it's time for the federal government to find a way to put the brakes on AI development if it's needed. "We request that the U.S. government support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development," reads an open letter signed by more than 1,100 AI workers from companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta. The letter zeroes in on "automated AI development," which refers to when AI will be capable of developing itself, something the industry calls "Recursive Self-Improvement." Anthropic has shared that its Claude models are quickly approaching that threshold. Look out for an alert in your inbox the next time a new story is published!

items.title: Another WTF moment.
items.summary:
Another WTF moment.

Hugging Face just open-sourced the fully local answer to OpenAI's Realtime voice API.

It's called speech-to-speech. You pip install it, run one command, and you get a WebSocket server at /v1/realtime that speaks the exact same protocol as OpenAI. Any client built for the OpenAI Realtime API can point at your machine instead and never know the difference.

This isn't a toy. The same pipeline runs in production as the conversation backend for thousands of Reachy Mini robots.

The stack is a four-stage cascade. Voice activity detection, speech to text, language model, text to speech. Each stage runs in its own thread with queues between them. Every stage is swappable via CLI flags.

Defaults out of the box are Silero VAD v5 for turn detection, NVIDIA's Parakeet TDT for transcription, and Qwen3-TTS for speech synthesis. The LLM slot points at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Hosted OpenAI, HF Inference Providers, OpenRouter, or a vLLM or llama.cpp server on your own hardware.

Swap components for your use case. Whisper, Faster Whisper, Lightning Whisper MLX, or Paraformer for STT. Kokoro-82M, Pocket TTS, ChatTTS, or MMS TTS for the voice. mlx-lm on Apple Silicon or Transformers on CUDA if you want the LLM in-process too.

Language coverage tracks whichever backends you pick. Parakeet TDT alone covers 25 European languages. Set --language auto and the STT auto-detects each spoken prompt and forwards it downstream. Set a specific code and the whole pipeline locks to that language.

Four run modes ship in the box. Realtime for the OpenAI-compatible WebSocket server. Local to talk through your machine's mic and speakers with no client at all. Raw WebSocket for a minimal custom client. Or a TCP socket mode where models run on a remote server and a thin client handles mic and playback.

The fully local recipe is two terminals. One runs llama.cpp serving Gemma 4. The other runs speech-to-speech pointed at that endpoint. No API keys. No network hops. No audio leaving the machine.

Apache 2.0 licensed. Python 3.10+. Docker compose file included. Sitting at 6.3k stars.

The thing worth understanding is what this really is. The Realtime API is becoming the default interface for voice agents. Hugging Face just released an open-source implementation of the server side that runs on your hardware, keeps your audio local, and lets you swap the model behind it every day if you want.

Every voice agent product being built right now assumes a paid API. This flips that assumption.

items.title: Lilian Weng shared today that she is leaving Thinking Machines Lab to focus on her health.
items.summary:
Lilian Weng shared today that she is leaving Thinking Machines Lab to focus on her health.

I went back to this 2019 talk at OpenAI. In front of 100+ women in tech, she made a difficult frontier problem, teaching a robotic hand dexterous manipulation through reinforcement learning and domain randomization, feel understandable and worth exploring.

That has always been part of Lilian’s impact. She didn’t just help build important systems. Through talks like this and Lil’Log, she opened up frontier research to an entire generation of researchers and builders.

Wishing her the time and space to recover.

As Lilian wrote today: “The future worth building is human.”

items.title: I asked @jxnlco (DevEx at OpenAI): “What’s the craziest thing Codex did for you?”
items.summary:
I asked @jxnlco (DevEx at OpenAI): “What’s the craziest thing Codex did for you?”

Here’s his answer:

“I was on a bike ride when a coworker asked me to fix a launch video. So I connected remotely from my phone and asked Codex to use computer use to edit the video, export it, and post it back to Slack.

Twenty minutes later, there was a new video in the Slack thread. Then I told Codex:

‘Every 30 minutes, check the thread for feedback and export V2, V3, V4.’

By the time I got home, the launch video was greenlit.”

Codex had handled the revisions by repeatedly checking Slack for feedback.

📌 Watch the full episode here: https://t.co/DulNtYvqGD

items.title: Gilbert Strang, a quiet MIT professor, picked up a piece of chalk and explained the one skill standing between you and e
items.summary:
Gilbert Strang, a quiet MIT professor, picked up a piece of chalk and explained the one skill standing between you and every account you have ever blown.

MIT put the entire course online. it has been free for over twenty years. almost nobody finishes it.

His point: the market never pays in certainties. it pays in probabilities, and a human gut can barely hold one straight. the math that holds ten thousand at once, weighs them, and collapses them into a single call is linear algebra. it is the branch Citadel and OpenAI both pay $400K to hire for.

he is not a trading guru. his 18.06 lectures are the most watched math class on the planet.

Skip to where he turns a wall of numbers into one vector. a single object carrying a thousand odds at once, in notation a beginner can follow.

No slides. no jargon. one piece of chalk.

a quant I know rewatches lecture one every year before he sizes a single position.

You do not have a strategy problem. you have a math problem. the fix has been free for two decades, and you are still guessing.

items.title: Moburst develops AI engine optimization capabilities for established companies - TechCrunch
items.summary: Mobile growth agency Moburst has built out a dedicated AI Engine Optimization practice aimed at established companies with existing app portfolios, betting that the category still lacks agencies with real depth rather than a rebranded service page. AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. For established companies vetting an AEO partner, the practical test is whether the agency can point to specific app-store-side work, not just web content changes, and whether it can describe a concrete process for reconciling inconsistent brand descriptions across many independent sources rather than treating that as someone else’s problem.

results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
Dưới đây là một hàm Python tính số Fibonacci bằng phương pháp đệ quy (recursion):

```python
def fibonacci(n):
    """
    Tính số Fibonacci thứ n bằng đệ quy.

    Args:
        n (int): Vị trí của số Fibonacci cần tính.

    Returns:
        int: Số Fibonacci thứ n.

    Raises:
        ValueError: Nếu n < 0.
    """
    if n < 0:
        raise ValueError("n phải là một số nguyên không âm")
    elif n == 0:
        return 0
    elif n == 1:
        return 1
    else:
        return fibonacci(n-1) + fibonacci(n-2)

# Ví dụ sử dụng
n = 10
print(f"Số Fibonacci thứ {n} là: {fibonacci(n)}")
```

Tuy nhiên, cần lưu ý rằng cách implement này không hiệu quả cho các giá trị `n` lớn do sự trùng lặp trong tính toán. Một cách tối ưu hơn là sử dụng kỹ thuật "memoization" để lưu trữ kết quả của các lần tính toán trước đó.

```python
def fibonacci_memo(n, memo={}):
    """
    Tính số Fibonacci thứ n bằng đệ quy với memoization.

    Args:
        n (int): Vị trí của số Fibonacci cần tính.
        memo (dict, optional): Dictionary lưu trữ kết quả tính toán trước đó. Defaults to {}.

    Returns:
        int: Số Fibonacci thứ n.
    """
    if n < 0:
        raise ValueError("n phải là một số nguyên không âm")
    elif n == 0:
        return 0
    elif n == 1:
        return 1
    elif n not in memo:
        memo[n] = fibonacci_memo(n-1, memo) + fibonacci_memo(n-2, memo)
    return memo[n]

# Ví dụ sử dụng
n = 10
print(f"Số Fibonacci thứ {n} là: {fibonacci_memo(n)}")
```

Cách implement thứ hai này sẽ hiệu quả hơn cho các giá trị `n` lớn.

Healthcare robotics faces critical challenges in data scarcity, generalization, and development velocity due to limited access to annotated demonstrations, the prevalence of rare but clinically important scenarios, and slow, resource-intensive prototyping cycles. [...] AI-generated content may summarize information incompletely. Verify important information. Learn more

Unlike autonomous driving or industrial robotics, healthcare robotics can’t rely on internet-scale data collection or unlimited real-world experimentation. Every demonstration requires specialized equipment, clinical expertise, and access to patients or laboratory environments. This creates three fundamental challenges for developers. [...] The third challenge is development velocity. Medical robotics development relies on benchtop phantoms, cadaver studies, animal models, and limited clinical evaluations. items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.

items.title: OpenAI's $1 Trillion IPO Ambition Faces New Timing Test as Anthropic Gains Ground - Dailyhunt
items.summary: **OpenAI** may be pushing back its public debut as it weighs whether market conditions can support its reported goal of a $1 trillion valuation. The analysts noted that OpenAI's decision on timing effectively acts as a pricing signal: management must choose between going public sooner at a potentially discounted valuation or waiting longer in hopes of reaching the $1 trillion mark. Despite OpenAI's higher valuation (private market valuations of $852 billion), PitchBook ($965 billion) suggested Anthropic currently commands a more attractive valuation relative to its business quality score. PitchBook said investors should watch for OpenAI to convert its confidential filing into a public S-1, the pricing of its employee tender offer, SpaceX’s Aug. 6 earnings and lockup timeline, and whether Anthropic proceeds with an October IPO. The firm said its outlook would change if OpenAI moves ahead with a 2026 IPO or if its public S-1 shows investors are willing to support a $1 trillion valuation sooner than expected.

items.title: OpenAI's rogue models roamed the internet for 4 days and staged a second attack - Politico
items.summary: GLOBAL POLITICS & POLICY 4 items. A second AI company confirmed that one of its customers was also targeted by OpenAI’s models. The powerful artificial intelligence models from OpenAI that went rogue and mounted an unprecedented, autonomous cyberattack earlier this month spent more than four days loose on the internet orchestrating the hack, according to a new analysis from the platform that was breached. Separately, a second AI company confirmed that one of its customers was also targeted by OpenAI’s models during the same event, raising questions about how OpenAI failed to detect the alarming activity for days. But in a new analysis published Tuesday, Hugging Face said OpenAI’s two models — one publicly released and a second unreleased — did much more: They carried out 17,600 hacking actions on the internet between July 9 and July 13, during which time the models moved from their first foothold on the open internet to inside Hugging Face’s servers.

OpenAI said Tuesday that the rogue AI agent that breached Hugging Face’s platform also hacked multiple third-party accounts and services as part of the attack. It's now clear that the unprecedented security incident, which arose during an internal test of OpenAI’s latest AI models, was more extensive than the company initially disclosed. In an updated blog post, OpenAI said that an ongoing review of the incident revealed that “four accounts” tied to “publicly available services” were used by the AI agent as part of a larger effort to hack Hugging Face. One of the additional accounts compromised by OpenAI’s agent was used as an “outbound relay and staging path,” potentially to obscure where the attack on Hugging Face was coming from, the company said. Reuters reported on Tuesday that a customer of Modal, a company that offers software infrastructure for training and running AI services, was one of the entities compromised by OpenAI’s agent.
